subject.title: [bug] Cannot publish new version of existing code plugin: API rejects with "packageId: invalid value; releaseId: invalid value"

question: Should code-plugin package publishes be fixed by widening pending-response support and repairing worker finalization only, or should maintainers also approve an emergency bypass for staged prepublication?
rationale: The observable bug is source-backed, but one proposed remedy bypasses a prepublication security gate and production worker health may require operator intervention outside a normal code-only repair.

options.title: Repair staging and pending response
options.body: Update package publish schemas/CLI handling for pending attempts and fix or validate worker finalization so clean package releases complete without bypassing the gate.

options.title: Add an explicit package bypass
options.body: Extend an emergency bypass to package publishes with clear audit, docs, and tests, accepting that this weakens prepublication gating when used.

options.title: Operator-only mitigation
options.body: Keep code unchanged for now and have maintainers inspect production publishAttempts/worker logs or temporarily change the staging flag.

recommendation.title: Repair staging and pending response
recommendation.body: Update package publish schemas/CLI handling for pending attempts and fix or validate worker finalization so clean package releases complete without bypassing the gate.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the staged prepublication path and worker that govern the security boundary in question.
